video.title: Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft Pick 11 - [9 Cat H2H Tyrese Maxey]

summary: Josh Lloyd runs a 12-team, 9-category mock draft from pick 11 and opens with Tyrese Maxey. He admits he is lower on Maxey than most and thinks Maxey could finish around 15th to 19th. His team is Maxey, Scottie Barnes (a panic pick when his timer ran out), Anthony Davis, Jaren Jackson Jr., Ryan Rollins, Desmond Bane, Ty Jerome, De'Aaron Fox, Brandin Podziemski, Darius Acuff Jr., Fred VanVleet, Kevin Porter Jr., Isaiah Jackson and Jalen Smith. He sees Damian Lillard and Paul George as top-30 players you can usually get late, but both were taken before his picks came up. His team projected 10th, but the standings were tightly bunched (48.5 projected wins against 51 for second place), and he calls it one of the most competitive mocks he has done. He also says ADP is not a fixed order, and if a player goes earlier than you want, you can take someone else later.

rules.text: Most second-round players are roughly interchangeable.
rules.quote: I think most of these second round guys are sort of relatively interchangeable

rules.text: You don't need any one specific player. If a target goes too early, take someone else later. When players go early, others get pushed back, so you will not run out of options.
rules.quote: You don't have to have that player. If he goes too early, just get somebody different later.

rules.text: Picking near the turn with two players you want is hard. You take one and hope the other comes back, but you cannot predict what the manager on the turn will do.
rules.quote: you hope the other one comes back around, but you just don't know what the bloke on the turn

rules.text: Late in drafts, choose between a high-upside player and a safer player who is more likely to finish ahead. He prefers the player with the bigger chance of finishing well above his draft spot.
rules.quote: the difference between those two statements is how you want to approach your team. That's your call

rules.text: Late rounds are flyer territory. He is happy to take upside flyers there.
rules.quote: This is flyer territory, too. So, I'm happy to take flyers on blokes.

rules.text: A pick that looks early is fine if it is within reasonable ranges. Player values vary a lot because of small factors, so draft order does not have to be fixed.
rules.quote: there's so much variance on players' values based on such small things

rules.text: Low-scoring big men are fine in category formats.
rules.quote: Going to be a pretty low-scoring player, I think, Isaiah. But, that's look again, it's fine in a category format.

rules.text: Players' values change from mock to mock depending on who is in the draft and how people are thinking.
rules.quote: the values of players change all  the time anyway, depending on who's in the draft

rules.text: In a competitive draft, projected standings are tightly bunched, so a low projected finish does not mean much.
rules.quote: the projected standings and records for these  teams in my league is so narrowly clustered
